findings.where: First screen, the hero photograph on the right (desktop-01), and the photograph above the line on phone (phone-01)
findings.fault: The brief for this direction, 'Mark at work', asks for a full-bleed photograph of Mark speaking, in real light. What the hero shows is Mark's head and shoulders cut out of their backdrop and set on flat slate, larger than life. The lectern, the room and the light of the event are all keyed away, and only a sliver of microphone is left at the bottom edge. So the scene no longer shows him at work. It looks like a floating head-and-shoulders cutout on a dark field, much like the 'dark ground' and 'portrait' directions. At this scale it also reads like a campaign poster rather than a refined advisor's page. On phone the head floats at the top with the line pressed up against its chin, which makes the cutout look stronger still.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who judges the first screen first and needs this direction to show its own idea (Mark seen in action, real people in real light) against the six others. Mark too, whose 'refined, never slick or salesy' tone a giant cut-out face undercuts. This is about the cutout and the scale the candidate chose, not about the stand-in photo itself.

findings.where: The header lockup on the first screen ('Mark M. Moseley' beside the mark), and the same pairing in the footer
findings.fault: The brief says his name leads, with the logo beside it. At a squint, the logo wins: the white arches and 'MMM INFRA' are bigger and heavier than the name, which is set small and light at about nav size. In the footer the gap is wider still. A large grey-and-blue mark sits over the name, which appears only as a small sans line before the email address. On both, the firm reads first and the person second.
findings.who_objects: The founder, applying the personal-advisor test that comes before craft ('the firm is the brand' fails, brand sheet §5). Also a bank officer arriving from LinkedIn, who is looking for Mark by name and finds a firm mark first.

findings.where: Article specimen, the lecture row at its foot ('Streamlining the PPP Process… Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF'), which 'Articles and talks' in the nav leads to
findings.fault: The research names the talks and PDF list as the product a visitor finds after the first look. Here it is one row with no heading, in small type, inside the article's own column straight after its last sentence. It looks like an attachment to that blog post, not the start of a list of his talks. A visitor who clicks 'Articles and talks' lands on this row and has no sign that it is the talks list.
findings.who_objects: Development-bank staff weighing an advisor, who read his talks and papers as evidence of his judgement (first-visit trust items 3 and 4, 'Feel the CV': the newest talk with its venue on the home page). They would miss it or think it is just this post's download.

findings.where: First screen, the 'Placeholder: Mark's photo from the current site…' caption, bottom left under the action (desktop-01), and under the action on phone (phone-01)
findings.fault: The caption belongs to the photograph, but it sits in the left text column under the email button, far from the photo. By proximity it reads as a note on the action or the text column. On phone it sits below the button, a whole screen away from the photo at the top.
findings.who_objects: The founder and other reviewers, who need to see at a glance which image is the stand-in. This placement makes the caption look like it labels the contact block instead.
